title: The tube lemma: an open neighbourhood of a product of quasi-compact subsets contains a product of open neighbourhoods

standard_prerequisites.name: The product topology and the notion of a basic open neighbourhood of a point of the product, together with the quasi-compactness of the two factors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's sections on products and on quasi-compact spaces, before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the basic product neighbourhoods used at the start of the proof and the finite subcovers extracted from the two quasi-compact sets.

core_obligations: Pointwise separation inside the open set: for each pair of points of the two quasi-compact subsets the proof chooses a basic product neighbourhood contained in the given open set W (proof lines 3269-3271).
Compactness in the first factor: fixing a point of the second subset, the proof extracts finitely many of the first factors covering the whole first subset (proof lines 3272-3276).

Compactness in the second factor: varying the point of the second subset and using the corresponding open neighbourhoods, the proof extracts finitely many of them covering the second subset, intersecting the first factors as it goes (proof lines 3276-3286).

Conclusion: the intersection of the finitely many first factors and the union of the finitely many second factors give open sets whose product contains the two quasi-compact subsets and lies in W (proof lines 3286-3288).
proof_roadmap: 先对 A×B 的每点取含于 W 的基本开积邻域 U_(a,b)×V_(a,b)。
固定 b 用 A 的紧性取有限多个 U 覆盖 A；再让 b 变动、用 B 的紧性取有限多个相应邻域覆盖 B，同时把对应的 U 取交，得到 U×V ⊂ W。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the tube lemma in the form this chapter uses (author lemma at source lines 3259-3266, label lemma-tube, bearing the author's own bracketed name): if a product of two quasi-compact subsets lies in an open subset of the product space, then it is contained in a product of open neighbourhoods still lying in that open subset. The proof (source lines 3268-3288) is the classical two-stage compactness argument: it starts from basic product neighbourhoods of the individual pairs, extracts a finite cover in the first factor after fixing a point of the second, and then extracts a finite cover in the second factor while intersecting the corresponding first factors (proof lines 3272-3286). The lemma is the tool by which properness of maps is characterised earlier in the same section. H2.
